A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fira and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the substantial appendix reorganization, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Fira pre-training, commonsense fine-tuning and ablation results in Section 5, plus scaling-factor analyses and simulations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original Fira experiments and adds resource measurements, MMLU evaluation, additional comparisons, sensitivity analyses and gradient-noise experiments.

M1.justification: The main Fira update, column-wise scaling, norm-growth limiter and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v3 introduces the diagnostic Fira-only-scaling variant, which removes the separate projected Adam update and applies low-rank-derived scaling directly to the full gradient (Appendices E.1 and F). This is a limited procedural addition used for analysis.

E1.justification: v3 retains C4 pre-training and the eight commonsense datasets, and adds MMLU evaluation covering STEM, social sciences, humanities and other subjects (Appendix J, Table 16). This substantially extends task coverage into multidisciplinary knowledge evaluation.

E2.justification: The commonsense comparison replaces Prefix, Series Adapter and Parallel Adapter with ReLoRA, Flora and full-rank training. Appendix J additionally compares Adam-mini, SlimAdam and FRUGAL on C4 and commonsense tasks, and APOLLO on MMLU. Adam is added to Figure 2, while new stabilization comparisons evaluate gradient shrink and tensor-wise scaling.

E3.justification: v3 replaces ten-matrix ranking comparisons with analyses across all matrices and sampled columns of 60M–1B models, adding similarity metrics and temporal comparisons. New evaluations introduce measured memory/throughput, gradient-noise injection, Gemma/Mistral configurations and Adagrad. Memory accounting adds gradients and includes previously excluded fine-tuning weights. The fine-tuning settings explicitly change AdamW to Adam (v1 Table 6 versus v3 Table 7), without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retained ablations, v3 tests alternative stabilization methods, limiter-threshold sensitivity, and the effects of scaling granularity, SVD and rank in Fira-only-scaling. Appendices D and F expand scaling-similarity and convergence analyses. Appendix K adds Gaussian-gradient-noise robustness testing against Adam.

E5.justification: v1 already reports Spearman and Kendall correlations with p-values. v3 adds Pearson correlations and corresponding significance reporting, and specifies shared random initialization for paired low-rank/full-rank comparisons (Appendix D, Table 10). It does not add repeated-seed performance uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Shared main-table perplexities and accuracies are retained, but v3 adds extensive benchmark, resource and analytical results. Table 20 newly reports noisy-gradient perplexities of 34.64 for Fira-only-scaling and 445.47 for Adam. Revised memory estimates use different accounting, rather than demonstrating resource regressions. The commonsense win count rises from four to five through changed comparators. A new inconsistency remains: v3 Table 18 reports Fira's 350M perplexity as 17.03, versus 16.85 retained in Table 3.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds an approximation-error definition, bounded-scaling assumption, theorem and proof connecting scaling-factor error to correction variability and captured gradient energy. The derivation explicitly simplifies projection to component sampling. The earlier variance theorem and proof are retained, moving from v1 Appendix A.1 to v3 Appendix E.2.

C1.justification: The central contribution of full-rank training under low-rank optimizer constraints remains. However, v3's abstract and contribution list omit v1's broad statement of matching or outperforming full-rank training, although specific comparisons remain in the body. The 7B headline changes from an eightfold smaller rank to eightfold smaller optimizer-state memory.

C2.justification: v3 expands explanations of why scaling-based updates differ from Adam and may outperform it, and explicitly frames the limiter as addressing instability introduced by the approximation. It adds interpretations concerning stabilization alternatives, gradient-noise robustness and optimization landscapes (Appendices F–K). Appendix L newly identifies the restriction to LLMs and untested applicability to multimodal and diffusion models.

D1.justification: Most algorithm documentation and training hyperparameters are retained. v3 updates the code pointer from Fira2024 to Fira, promises a Python library, and documents additional details such as ZeRO2 for full-fine-tuning resource measurements, column sampling and the Gaussian-noise magnitude. These are limited additions rather than a comprehensive implementation revision.

R1.justification: Appendix I adds substantive positioning against Adam-mini, SlimAdam, MicroAdam, AdaLomo, FRUGAL and GaRare. APOLLO and alternative stabilization research also enter the discussion. This substantially expands methodological differentiation beyond v1's predominantly LoRA, GaLore and system-level memory-efficiency framing.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract and scaling-factor narrative, moves the main algorithm into a dedicated implementation appendix, and reorganizes v1's Appendix A.1–A.7 into separate implementation, settings, overhead, similarity and theory sections. The expanded appendix structure and rewritten explanations substantially change document organization beyond citation-style edits.

P2.justification: v1's scaling-factor heatmaps are replaced by similarity tables and new trend plots. Figure 2 gains an Adam curve, and the method-comparison table gains a full-rank column and gradient-memory row. Numerous resource, ablation and robustness displays are added, while algorithms and retained plots are relocated or resized within the revised layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens two central weaknesses in v1: scaling similarity supported mainly by ten matrix rankings, and efficiency supported only by memory estimates. Analyses across model sizes and columns, mechanism-focused ablations, and measured memory/throughput provide stronger scientific and practical evidence. Broader comparisons and robustness tests reinforce these gains. Reporting issues, particularly the conflicting 350M perplexities in Tables 3 and 18 and the unexplained optimizer-setting revision, temper but do not outweigh the improvement.
